title: Thrombin Needs a Surface
endLine: A clot grows only where a surface holds the enzymes.

scenes.tts: Last time, a global number came from a local reading: a kidney cell judged the oxygen in its own patch. A cut seals in minutes, while the same clotting proteins flow through every healthy vessel untouched. Where is the line drawn?
scenes.narration: Last time, a global number came from a local reading: a kidney cell judged the oxygen in its own patch. A cut seals in minutes, while the same clotting proteins flow through every healthy vessel untouched. Where is the line drawn?
scenes.caption: Last time, a global number came from a local reading: a kidney cell judged the oxygen in its own patch. A cut seals in minutes, while the same clotting proteins flow through every healthy vessel untouched. Where is the line drawn?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). Blood is carried over from the first film unchanged: RED red cells drifting left to right in pale AMBER plasma, with the vessel's inner lining a thin bright WHITE line. NEW COLOURS BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: the cells under the wall TAN, with short TAN studs for tissue factor; platelets VIOLET discs, gaining a GOLD rim when activated; thrombin MAGENTA dots; the two clotting complexes labelled block-pairs, GREEN and ORANGE; fibrin WHITE threads; the brakes on intact lining CYAN. LAYOUT, kept all film: one vessel runs left to right across the upper two thirds of the frame, filling about 60% of frame height, its WHITE lining intact except for a torn gap in the lower wall at centre; beneath that gap a TAN layer of cells with studs, out of contact with the blood on either side of the tear; at the right edge a vertical MAGENTA gauge labelled 'thrombin here', with a 'schematic' tag under it that stays all film. OPENING MOTION: during the link-back sentence, a faint ghost from the first film appears over the vessel for two seconds, a kidney patch with a tight CYAN halo and a small tag 'last time', then fades for good. On the second sentence, a VIOLET plug is already in place in the torn gap; the camera slides along the vessel to the right, past long stretches of intact WHITE lining where plasma and red cells pass with nothing happening, then slides back to the tear. On the question, white text across the top: 'Why only here?'

Title 'Thrombin Needs a Surface' fades in above the vessel for 2 s while the question text fades out beneath it. The flow continues: RED cells drift past, the VIOLET plug sits in the tear, and the MAGENTA gauge at the right rests empty at the bottom of its scale.

scenes.tts: The plug has already done one job. It anchored a membrane at the breach: activated platelets turn their phosphatidylserine outward, and so become a procoagulant surface.
scenes.narration: The plug has already done one job. It anchored a membrane at the breach: activated platelets turn their phosphatidylserine outward, and so become a procoagulant surface.
scenes.caption: The plug has already done one job. It anchored a membrane at the breach: activated platelets turn their phosphatidylserine outward, and so become a procoagulant surface.
scenes.visual: Push in on the tear until the plug fills about 65% of frame height; the flow and a stretch of WHITE lining stay in frame above it. The plug resolves into about five VIOLET platelet discs packed into the gap and held there as plasma streams past them without carrying them off. On 'turn their phosphatidylserine outward', each disc's rim transforms: small marks that pointed inward rotate to point outward and the rim lights up GOLD, one platelet after another, so the plug ends with a continuous GOLD edge facing the blood. Label on the plug, 5 words or fewer: 'procoagulant surface'. An arrow labelled 'held at the breach' points from the flow to the plug. Nothing else appears yet.

scenes.tts: Tissue factor sits on cells beneath the lining, out of contact with blood until the wall breaks. Exposed, it binds factor seven a, and that pair cuts factor ten and factor nine. Factor ten a with five a makes a little thrombin.
scenes.narration: Tissue factor sits on cells beneath the lining, out of contact with blood until the wall breaks. Exposed, it binds factor VIIa, and that pair cuts factor X and factor IX. Factor Xa with Va makes a little thrombin.
scenes.caption: Tissue factor sits on cells beneath the lining, out of contact with blood until the wall breaks. Exposed, it binds factor VIIa, and that pair cuts factor X and factor IX. Factor Xa with Va makes a little thrombin.
scenes.visual: Camera slides down from the plug to the TAN layer under the tear, which now fills the lower half of the frame; the plug stays visible at the top of frame with its GOLD edge. On the first sentence, a ghost replay shows the wall intact, with the TAN studs covered by the WHITE lining and plasma passing above, then the lining tears again and plasma reaches the studs. Label on a stud: 'tissue factor'. On 'binds factor seven a', a labelled block 'VIIa' drifts out of the plasma and clicks onto a stud. On 'cuts factor ten and factor nine', two plain blocks labelled 'X' and 'IX' arrive at the pair, each leaves with a small notch and a new label, 'Xa' and 'IXa'. On the last sentence, 'Xa' pairs with a block 'Va' on the TAN cell and a thin stream of MAGENTA dots rises from it; the MAGENTA gauge at the right fills only a short way up its scale and stops, labelled 'trickle'.

scenes.tts: Nowhere near enough to clot anything, and it does not last: tissue factor pathway inhibitor shuts that assembly down. The trickle was never meant to clot blood. It is a signal: it activates platelets and cuts factors five, eight and eleven.
scenes.narration: Nowhere near enough to clot anything, and it does not last: tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI) shuts that assembly down. The trickle was never meant to clot blood. It is a signal: it activates platelets and cuts factors V, VIII and XI.
scenes.caption: Nowhere near enough to clot anything, and it does not last: tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI) shuts that assembly down. The trickle was never meant to clot blood. It is a signal: it activates platelets and cuts factors V, VIII and XI.
scenes.visual: Keep the TAN cell at the bottom and the plug at the top in one frame. On 'nowhere near enough', the MAGENTA gauge's short fill is bracketed against the rest of its empty scale, labelled 'not enough'. On 'shuts that assembly down', a CYAN block labelled 'TFPI' slides onto the tissue factor, VIIa and Xa group; the group dims and the MAGENTA stream from it stops. On 'it is a signal', the MAGENTA dots already released travel up to the plug instead of fading: as they land, the remaining VIOLET platelets gain their GOLD rims, and three plasma blocks arriving at the plug are each cut and relabelled in turn, 'V' to 'Va', 'VIII' to 'VIIIa', 'XI' to 'XIa', with the VIII block visibly leaving a carrier block behind as it is cut. The gauge holds at its low level throughout this scene.

scenes.tts: Thrombin has built the machine that makes thrombin in bulk, and it assembles on the platelet membrane. Factor nine a with eight a makes factor ten a, and ten a with five a cuts prothrombin. On the usual estimate, well over ninety percent of a wound's thrombin is made there.
scenes.narration: Thrombin has built the machine that makes thrombin in bulk, and it assembles on the platelet membrane. Factor IXa with VIIIa makes factor Xa, and Xa with Va cuts prothrombin. On the usual estimate, well over 90 percent of a wound's thrombin is made there.
scenes.caption: Thrombin has built the machine that makes thrombin in bulk, and it assembles on the platelet membrane. Factor IXa with VIIIa makes factor Xa, and Xa with Va cuts prothrombin. On the usual estimate, well over 90 percent of a wound's thrombin is made there.
scenes.visual: Push in on the plug so its GOLD edge fills the frame, the TAN layer small at the bottom. Two labelled block-pairs settle onto the GOLD edge and stay there: a GREEN pair 'IXa + VIIIa' and an ORANGE pair 'Xa + Va'. The IXa block arrives from the TAN cell below, the VIIIa, Va and prothrombin blocks from the plasma. The GREEN pair turns out 'Xa' blocks that slide a short distance along the same edge into the ORANGE pair; the ORANGE pair cuts arriving prothrombin blocks and releases MAGENTA dots in a thick plume. The MAGENTA gauge at the right climbs quickly from its trickle level to near the top of its scale, and a faint dashed tick marks where the trickle had stopped, labelled 'trickle'. On the last sentence, a simple split bar beside the gauge divides into a thin slice labelled 'on the tan cells' and a long slice labelled 'on platelets', with a small tag 'usual estimate'.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Thrombin is made on surfaces, not in solution. A clot grows where a surface holds the enzymes, and nowhere else.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Thrombin is made on surfaces, not in solution. A clot grows where a surface holds the enzymes, and nowhere else.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Thrombin is made on surfaces, not in solution. A clot grows where a surface holds the enzymes, and nowhere else.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole vessel, everything still flowing. On 'not in solution', loose ghost copies of the GREEN and ORANGE block-pairs appear out in midstream, drift apart into separate blocks, and are swept away downstream without making a single MAGENTA dot. On 'where a surface holds the enzymes', the camera settles on the two pairs still locked to the GOLD platelet edge, which pulse once together, and the MAGENTA plume above them brightens. A bracket spans the plug and the TAN layer under the tear, labelled 'surfaces'; long stretches of intact WHITE lining to the left and right stay plainly bare. Text across the top, 5 words or fewer: 'Made on a surface'.

scenes.tts: The burst does the visible work. Thrombin cuts fibrinogen to fibrin, a mesh through the plug. It activates factor thirteen, which cross-links the mesh against arterial pressure.
scenes.narration: The burst does the visible work. Thrombin cuts fibrinogen to fibrin, a mesh through the plug. It activates factor XIII, which cross-links the mesh against arterial pressure.
scenes.caption: The burst does the visible work. Thrombin cuts fibrinogen to fibrin, a mesh through the plug. It activates factor XIII, which cross-links the mesh against arterial pressure.
scenes.visual: Stay on the plug with the gauge near full. MAGENTA dots meet plasma blocks labelled 'fibrinogen'; each cut block transforms into a short WHITE thread, and the threads join end to end and knit into a mesh that fills the gaps between the VIOLET platelets. On 'factor thirteen', a labelled block 'XIII' is cut by a MAGENTA dot and then lays small WHITE cross-links between neighbouring threads, which visibly tighten the mesh. On the last clause, the pulse of the flow pushes against the sealed plug: before cross-linking a ghost of the loose mesh bulged outward, and the cross-linked mesh now barely moves. Label on the mesh: 'fibrin, cross-linked'.

scenes.tts: Thrombin made at the breach could drift downstream. Antithrombin destroys it, and on intact lining a surface sugar speeds antithrombin up by a hundred to a thousandfold. How far does thrombin get: a whole vessel, or a cell or two?
scenes.narration: Thrombin made at the breach could drift downstream. Antithrombin destroys it, and on intact lining a surface sugar speeds antithrombin up by a hundred to a thousandfold. How far does thrombin get: a whole vessel, or a cell or two?
scenes.caption: Thrombin made at the breach could drift downstream. Antithrombin destroys it, and on intact lining a surface sugar speeds antithrombin up by a hundred to a thousandfold. How far does thrombin get: a whole vessel, or a cell or two?
scenes.visual: Pull back so the plug sits at the left of frame and a long run of intact WHITE lining extends to the right. MAGENTA dots spill out of the plug into the flow and travel right. On 'antithrombin destroys it', CYAN blocks labelled 'antithrombin' drift in the plasma and extinguish MAGENTA dots on contact, slowly at first. On 'a surface sugar', a CYAN fringe grows along the inner face of the intact WHITE lining, labelled 'surface sugar', and the antithrombin blocks sitting on that fringe extinguish dots far faster, with a small speed chip beside them reading 'x100 to x1000'. On the question, a WHITE ruler lays itself along the vessel from the plug with two candidate marks only, one close to the plug and one far downstream, and white text across the top: 'How far does thrombin get?'

Predict pause. The question card and the two-mark ruler stay. Near-stillness by design: plasma drifts slowly, a few MAGENTA dots hover just outside the plug, the CYAN fringe shimmers faintly along the lining, and neither mark on the ruler is chosen. No other change.

scenes.tts: One to five micrometres. One to a few cell thicknesses, from diffusion and decay rates: an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measurement. In open plasma the reach is tens of micrometres, and flow only shortens it.
scenes.narration: One to five micrometres. One to a few cell thicknesses, from diffusion and decay rates: an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measurement. In open plasma the reach is tens of micrometres, and flow only shortens it.
scenes.caption: One to five micrometres. One to a few cell thicknesses, from diffusion and decay rates: an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measurement. In open plasma the reach is tens of micrometres, and flow only shortens it.
scenes.visual: The far mark on the ruler fades out; the near mark brightens and is labelled '1 to 5 micrometres'. The escaping MAGENTA dots are now extinguished within that short band, which is shaded faintly beside the plug. On 'a few cell thicknesses', the thin cross-sectional thickness of the lining wall is bracketed and shown to match the shaded band. A tag appears under the ruler and stays to the end of the scene: 'order-of-magnitude estimate'. On 'in open plasma', the CYAN fringe is hidden over one stretch and there the shaded band stretches about ten times longer, labelled 'tens of micrometres'; the fringe then returns and the band snaps back. On 'flow only shortens it', the flow speeds up and the shaded band contracts a little further.

scenes.tts: More brakes belong to the intact lining. Thrombomodulin turns thrombin into an activator of protein C, which inactivates factors five a and eight a. Prostacyclin and nitric oxide keep passing platelets quiet, and later plasmin dissolves the fibrin.
scenes.narration: More brakes belong to the intact lining. Thrombomodulin turns thrombin into an activator of protein C, which inactivates factors Va and VIIIa. Prostacyclin and nitric oxide keep passing platelets quiet, and later plasmin dissolves the fibrin.
scenes.caption: More brakes belong to the intact lining. Thrombomodulin turns thrombin into an activator of protein C, which inactivates factors Va and VIIIa. Prostacyclin and nitric oxide keep passing platelets quiet, and later plasmin dissolves the fibrin.
scenes.visual: Keep the plug at the left and the intact lining at the right. On 'thrombomodulin', a CYAN receptor labelled 'thrombomodulin' appears on the lining; a MAGENTA dot docks in it and changes colour to CYAN as it docks, then cuts a block labelled 'protein C', whose cut form travels to the plug and knocks the 'Va' and 'VIIIa' blocks out of the GREEN and ORANGE pairs, so the MAGENTA plume thins and the gauge drops a step. On 'prostacyclin and nitric oxide', two small CYAN puffs leave the lining and meet VIOLET platelets passing in the flow, which stay plain VIOLET with no GOLD rim and drift on by. On 'later plasmin', a day-and-hours clock ticks forward at the top, a CYAN block labelled 'plasmin' lands on the WHITE mesh and the threads shorten and disperse, leaving the lining whole as the flow returns.

scenes.tts: Read it back. The plug puts a surface where the wall breaks, the trickle switches it on, the burst happens there. That is why your finger clots while blood in your lung stays liquid.
scenes.narration: Read it back. The plug puts a surface where the wall breaks, the trickle switches it on, the burst happens there. That is why your finger clots while blood in your lung stays liquid.
scenes.caption: Read it back. The plug puts a surface where the wall breaks, the trickle switches it on, the burst happens there. That is why your finger clots while blood in your lung stays liquid.
scenes.visual: Rewind the world to the sealed-wound state and pull back to the whole vessel, everything moving. The three steps light up in order as they are named, each on the object that did it: the GOLD platelet edge in the tear, then the TAN studs with their thin MAGENTA stream, then the GREEN and ORANGE pairs on the GOLD edge with the gauge filling. On the last sentence, the frame divides into two panels of the SAME world: at the left the torn vessel with its plug, mesh and full gauge, at the right an untouched vessel of identical colours with an empty gauge, bare WHITE lining, loose unpaired blocks drifting past and RED cells flowing freely. Labels, 5 words or fewer: 'same proteins, both panels'.

End card over the dimmed but still moving two-panel world (red cells drifting in both, the MAGENTA gauge full at the left and empty at the right). Large centred white text: 'A clot grows only where a surface holds the enzymes.' The GOLD platelet edge and the GREEN and ORANGE block-pairs pulse once behind the line.
